pr_title: Fix synthetic source for flattened field when used with ignore_above
pr_body:
Previously if any leaf field in `flattened` field value was ignored due to `ignore_above` setting we would store the entire object in ignored source. This is not correct since it is possible that another object will be indexed which does not have any ignored leaf fields. Since ignored source takes precedence over native synthetic source, second object would be lost in such scenario.

This PR changes the approach to instead only store leaf values that are ignored in a dedicated stored field. When synthetic source is synthesized these values are merged with doc values to produce a document.

Closes #112044.

issue_context.title: Synthetic source is wrong for arrays of flattened fields containing subfields longer than ignore_above
comments:
It looks like `flattened` field type in general does not support correctly displaying arrays in synthetic source. Synthetic source is generated using doc_values of keyed field (`._keyed`) which encode a path to the field inside an object and its value in one byte array. The problem is that during parsing all object fields are simply added to the keyed field even if multiple objects are parsed in one document (e.g. with arrays or object arrays one level up in the document). During construction of synthetic source doc_values are retrieved and written, resulting in one giant object containing combined fields from all flattened values indexed.

Some options:
1. Disallow indexing multiple `flattened` values as we do for other field types. That seems quite strict but it is not clear what is the real usage of that.
2. Always set `synthetic_source_keep` to `arrays` for flattened fields. That does not however solve the problem of arrays being present on a higher level in the document.
3. Always use fallback synthetic source for `flattened`. Not ideal for disk space given we have most of the data in doc_values already. If it's rare enough could be okay.
4. Change doc_values format somehow to add missing information to distinguish different objects (not clear how).
5. Document it and leave it as is since it does not impact reindexing. Still needs a fix to synthetic source to handle ignore_above correctly.

I think this is the way synthetic source handles **arrays of objects**...which is "arrays are moved to leaves". See https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/mapping-source-field.html#synthetic-source-modifications-leaf-arrays

Can we just use `SortedSetDocValues` here directly instead of using an additional layer of abstraction? 

For example in `DocValuesSortedKeyedValues` we directly sorted set doc values instead of `DocValuesFieldValues` as an intermediate interface.
Do we need the `DocValuesFieldValues` interface at all? It is either no value or uses `SortedSetDocValues`. Maybe we always use `SortedSetDocValues` directly and in case of no value it is null?

I was actually looking at that too. I believe we can't directly use `SortedSetDocValues` because when there is no doc values, it contains an empty singleton which we don't expect. We could just set it to null indeed.

So `FlattenedFieldDocValuesLoader` also tracks if current document has doc values and i think inlining all this logic into `FlattenedSortedSetDocValuesSyntheticFieldLoader` reduces readability quite a bit. I'll keep this as is.
